content.thinking:
I'm planning the full module in one pass, designing a floating island diorama roughly 2.4 meters across with a grass-topped disc and rocky underside tapering down to touch the ground plane.

I'm fleshing out the scene elements—waterfall with mist fading near the base, three rounded toon trees, ruins with an arch, broken columns, steps, and a glowing crystal accent, plus a small feeding pond and scattered floating rocks with gold filigree trim.

For structure, I'm deciding to use a single root joint since nothing in the scene actually needs to move, with all parts attaching via position rather than extra joints.

Now I'm shaping the island itself: a lathed rock body tapering from a wide grassy top down to a jagged point near the base, using creased segments for a faceted stone look rather than smooth curves, with extra rock chunks scattered around the rim for irregularity, plus separate grass and soil cap layers defined by their own outline profiles.

For the rock's paint, I'll vary coloring by height—brownish soil near the top, mottled stone with tiny crystal flecks below—wrapped through the cel shading function so shadows derive automatically from the lit paint. The lathe tip meets y=0 cleanly, and the island's top surface sits around y=1.1 to set up the terrain shaping.

Now I'm positioning a pond slightly above the grass plane, deciding where the waterfall edge should sit relative to the camera's three-quarter view—placing it around 50° azimuth so it's visible—then planning a stream ribbon flowing from the pond across the grass to that edge, where a hanging flat box will form the waterfall sheet down to a lower height.

Checking that the fall clears the sloped rock beneath it, I confirm it drops freely in the air before ending in a mist puff near the base. Now I'm working out how to render the water itself—weighing a textured box slab against camera-facing cards with streak textures for the falling water surface.

I'll use hanging cards with a 180-degree lean so they drape straight down, oriented with their flow along the outward radial direction and width along the horizontal tangent, making them visible and double-sided from outside. I'm stacking a few offset cards for layered depth, plus adding a thin opaque box underneath as a solid core to give the water body some substance.

For that core box, I'm setting the section axes so thickness runs radially outward and width wraps tangentially, then painting a gradient that shifts from white-cyan near the top to deeper cyan further down using a mix function along the vertical coordinate.

Now I'm adding stripe texture via a grain pattern sized small and aligned along the vertical axis for a foam-streak look, then working out the waterfall's geometry: defining a frame with radial and tangential unit vectors, placing a fall start point above the pond, and sweeping a box-sectioned ribbon path from the pond edge up to the lip with tapering half-extents.

I'm placing the pond center with a polar-coordinate helper function, then building it as a short cylinder for the water surface with a ring of small stones around the rim, and considering lily pad cards floating on top.

I'm routing a curved river section using a Catmull-Rom spline through several points, giving it a tapered tube shape for the water channel, and figuring out spacing so the pond, river, and island ruins all fit without overlapping -- putting ruins toward the back-left and sizing the pond and river radii accordingly, plus adding paired stones along the riverbank.

Now I'm setting up the waterfall starting point at the island's lip.

For mist I'll use a cluster of simple white low-poly spheres for puffs, plus a flat torus for the ripple ring, and make sure falling droplets fade out before reaching y=0 so they land cleanly into the mist. Now I'm thinking about trees: curved brown trunk sweep with cel-shaded paint and canopy built from a few overlapping icosahedron shapes.

Still defining canopy geometry...

Now I'm sketching out the ruins layout itself—broken stone arches with mottled grass textures, warm cream stone, lavender shadow tones, and glowing cyan crystal accents for an anemo/hydro ruin feel, positioning the first column elements toward the back-left of the stage.

I'm working out the broken arch geometry, spanning the annulus sector from the left springing point up to near the top with jagged edges, sizing the inner and outer radii so the arch width aligns with the column spacing and outer column faces.

Working out how Paint's shading resolves within nested context, then sketching a stone block helper that layers moss mottling onto upward-facing surfaces.

Writing stone texture function...

Now moving to columns -- drafting a lathe profile with fluting detail for the shaft.

Now I'm planning the ruined wall section with stacked, rotated moss-covered blocks and a staircase of boxes leading to the gate, plus a fallen cylindrical drum. I want a glowing crystal floating between the columns on a pedestal, octahedron-shaped with a teal glow, maybe with orbiting smaller crystals for an anemo-shrine feel, positioned under the arch.

I'm also sketching out the trees: a twisting, sweeping trunk on the right with layered sphere canopies and leaf cards, plus a pink sakura-style blossom tree on the front-left with falling petal cards, and considering a third smaller tree.

Now I'm thinking through the remaining scenery -- adding a stacked-cone pine tree, bushes, flowers on stems, scattered grass tufts via textured cards, and mushrooms, while checking the overall scale works out to roughly 2.4m tall and wide with the crystal and floating rocks included.

For the grass tufts, I'm scattering card instances with a grass-blade texture across the island, rejecting positions too close to the pond, river, or ruins footprint, and keeping everything within the island's radius. I'm also planning small floating rock chunks orbiting beyond the rim with flattened grass caps on top, built through a reusable helper function.

I'm rethinking scale so the island stays within a reasonable 1.5-3m span, pulling the floating rocks inward to a tighter radius near the waterfall. Now I'm working out hanging vine cards along the overhang lip, positioning them in a ring, angling them to face upward and flow outward radially while skipping the waterfall gap.

For placement I'm indexing the vine cards by their azimuth position in the array, setting them slightly lower than the grass cap so they hang freely clear of the rock's narrowing underside. I'm also adding downward-pointing stalactite spikes scattered across the rock's underside for extra detail.

Now I'm computing a radius function for the rock profile to place teal crystal clusters on the underside, using octahedra oriented along an outward-downward normal and elongated vertically, with a glow effect applied. I'm also adding hanging tree roots that sweep downward from the rock surface with a tapered point, plus some gold filigree detailing.

I'm planning extra decorative touches too: a ring of rune dots around the arch, gold trim on columns and pedestal, a tasseled cloth hanging from the arch, and a small glowing stone lantern near the pond. For textures I need several SVGs -- leaf, blade, petal, vine, tassel, rune circle, mist -- kept simple, with leaf cards scattered across canopy spheres using frame-based placement and tinted two-tone green coloring, roughly sixty per tree.

Writing leaf SVG code...

For the leaf shape I'm using a grey-toned drawing so the tint system can recolor it correctly for both green and pink trees, adjusting stroke widths to match the raster resolution. Now I'm thinking through the ground paint helper for grass, planning lighter grass patches and scattered flower dots using a cell-based placement approach.

Still writing grass paint logic...

Now I'm scattering flower dots on top faces using a noise-based threshold, coloring petals white, yellow, or pink by id, and deciding the mud footpath isn't needed. For rock, I'm working out a strata-painting function that bands colors by height using noise-perturbed layers.

I want the underside to feel more jagged and dramatic, so I'm adding stalactite spikes, hanging crystals, and dangling roots. I'm plotting the rock's silhouette as a sequence of profile points that stay non-self-crossing, with a flat top edge closing back to the base axis, and noting the grass cap at the bottom will need to overlap the rock's top edge properly.

I'm checking that the dirt band near the rim (around y 0.86-0.97) stays visually consistent with the cap lip radius so nothing clips oddly, and keeping the grass top flat rather than mounded. Now I'm sketching a helper function to interpolate the rock's radius at any height from the profile points, then planning the overall code structure—imports for the geometry builder, framing, noise, cell patterns, color mixing, paint, and grain utilities needed to compose the full scene.

Writing imports and setup...

Adding more helper functions...

Finishing the profile points for the rock outline, then closing it with a point back at (0, 0.97) to form the lathe shape, using flat shading since segment count is under 12.

For the grass cap, I'm checking that a differing segment count between the rock (11-gon) and cap (12-gon or 14) won't cause a visible radius mismatch at the seam, comparing their polygon vertex radii at matching heights to see if they align closely enough.

I'll settle on 10 segments for both rock and cap, giving a low-poly decagon look that reads as toon-style, and plan to add rim chunk rocks and stalactite spikes around the edges to break up the silhouette.

Spikes get placed using positions sampled from the rock surface via polar coordinates at reduced radius, aiming downward. For crystal clusters, I'm defining a helper that builds an octahedron scaled along its axis toward a given direction and applies a glow effect, using flat string colors since glow requires simple fills.

For roots, I'm sweeping catmull-rom curves running from rock surface points downward with tapering radius, using flat start caps and pointed end caps to simulate hanging root strands.

Now I'm sketching out a tree builder function that constructs a trunk via a leaning catmull curve with tapering radius, adds small root flares at the base, generates branch sweeps toward canopy centers, and places clustered spheres at the canopy top colored with leaf cel paint for foliage.

For each canopy ball I'm scattering leaf cards across the upper hemisphere using a fibonacci point distribution, building a frame at each point oriented along its outward direction, then sizing and angling the leaf cards with some spin and bend variation so they read as foliage lit from the frame's normal.

I'm also setting up pine trees as tiered cones, bushes as ball clusters with berries, and flowers made from stems with small spherical petal clusters, planning around 14 flowers per instance.

I need to watch my mesh budget though—each distinct card texture call creates its own mesh, so with ruins, trees, and many flower parts I could blow past my 1000-part limit. Instead of building each flower from separate stem/center/petal meshes, I'm switching to flat SVG card textures for flower heads, generating a few colored flower variants with a function that draws petals and center together so each flower only costs one card draw.

I'm scattering grass tufts as double-sided cards with a two-tone green gradient texture across roughly 110 positions, and now I'm laying out the ruined gate geometry—column positions, heights, and the arch springing from the column tops up to a peak around y=2.2, roughly matching the tree heights so the scene reads proportionally.

With the right column broken shorter, I'm leaving the arch incomplete on that side and adding a fallen stone fragment lying nearby to suggest collapse, then extruding the arch shape and painting voussoir lines across its surface using angle-based segmentation.

I could add a thin gold border near the inner arc edge, using the radial distance to mark a narrow band around r≈0.24-0.25 as a gold trim accent on the stone faces.

For the column, I'm thinking about using the lathe outline's vertical position to paint gold bands at specific height ranges, keeping flutes as darker stone lines elsewhere.

I'm adding moss near the base using position and noise checks, then wrapping a non-cel stone paint factory with a cel-shaded version for the column. I also need to make sure unused parameters in paint functions are prefixed with underscore to avoid lint issues, then move on to adding a rune circle decal as an upward-facing plane at the base with a glowing texture.

I'm placing the rune decal at the gate center with steps positioned in front so they don't overlap it, then designing the rune texture itself—a circular SVG with teal and gold strokes and tick marks radiating around the ring, followed by starting a lathe-based pedestal profile at the same center point.

Now I'm adding a floating crystal above the pedestal: a teal octahedron with glow plus smaller orbiting crystals, surrounded by tilted gold torus rings, then building out the stone steps and a fallen column drum lying on its side nearby.

Using rotation [0, yaw, 90] to get fallen cylinders lying at varied angles. For the scene, I'm adding a low broken wall of randomly sized stone blocks along one edge, and placing a stone lantern near the pond's edge at a calculated position.

Now I'm designing the lantern itself—base, post, glowing window box, cone roof, and finial—then building the pond as a flat water disc with a radial color gradient painted by distance from center to fake a glowing ring effect.

Still shaping the river path...

I'm checking that the pond radius covers the river's starting point correctly, then sketching the waterfall path with points descending from the pond edge down to the base, using a tapering radius for the width as it falls.

For the orientation along the fall, I'm setting the initial up-vector vertically and letting it parallel-transport so it rotates outward as the path curves downward. Then I'm adding streak-based paint for the falling water using noise along the lateral coordinate, plus white foam highlighting near the edges.

Adding thin foam strand sweeps...

I'm also layering in misty atmosphere near the waterfall base — soft white-cyan cloud blobs and scattered spray droplet spheres along the fall tail, keeping everything positioned above ground level so the mist settles naturally around the bottom tip.

Now I'm placing three floating rocks around the scene using a helper that builds each as a flattened dodecahedron with a green cap, a spiky underside, a small crystal accent, and scattered debris pebbles — varying their positions, scale, and height so they feel organically distributed.

Checking the overall bounding width, I tweak the radius down slightly to keep the composition within the target size. Then I move on to hanging vine and tassel details: adding leafy vine textures along the lip ring, gold tassels dangling from the arch's inner top, and a teal cloth banner with a gold emblem for the gate.

I decide to skip birds, but add a small mushroom cluster near the trees using cylinder stems with hemisphere caps, plain red-pink coloring plus a few tiny white spheres instead of painted spots. I set the grass tuft count to roughly 90, scatter flower cards randomly across 24 spots using three texture variants, and define a blocked-area check that excludes placement near the pond and river so decorations don't overlap water features.

I'm now mapping out the exclusion boxes around the ruins footprint, wall segment, tree trunks, and lantern, plus pinning down final tree positions and radii for the oak, blossom tree, and pine/rock so the scatter logic avoids them properly.

Also repositioning tree1 near (0.5,-0.5). For the oak canopy, I'm sizing the cluster of spheres around the trunk top so the overall tree height lands near 2.35, keeping it under the gate's 2.2 height with some margin, and factoring in the floating rocks up to 1.9. Now I'm defining the tree function's parameters for position, trunk height, lean, and canopy sphere layout.

Writing trunk path and buttress roots...

Now I'm figuring out card distribution on each canopy ball - roughly 28 cards for a radius-0.3 ball, sized around 0.15-0.18, using a lighter tinted color like a soft green over a white leaf texture so the grey base multiplies into the right hue.

For the pine tree I'm stacking four cone tiers of decreasing size on a trunk, topped with a tiny glowing teal bauble instead of a star. Bushes get three green cel-shaded spheres plus a few pink flower dots, and I'm adding scattered boulders and pebbles near the wall along with a gold-filigree stone tablet detail.

I'm placing a stele near the wall with a front decal of symmetrical gold scroll filigree, positioning the plane just in front of the tablet face and scaling the SVG viewBox to fit.

I'm adjusting positions: moving the first tree slightly outward, double-checking wall and stele coordinates, and deciding to skip reeds near the pond for now.

Now I'm writing the typed frame and card-placement helper functions, making sure array types are explicit to satisfy strict typing.

Still writing scattering logic...

Still writing scatter and grass placement logic...

Still writing flower petal SVG and sizing...

Now I'm adding falling petals around the blossom tree as small pink card frames facing upward with random lean and spin, scattered through the air at varying heights. I'm also considering adding soft cloud puffs beneath the floating island near its base to soften the transition between rock and sky.

Deciding to skip a decorative gold ring around the island's rim since it feels unnatural, saving gold trim details for ruins and lantern roofs instead. Now I'm starting to define the color palette constants for grass, dirt, and other materials before writing out the stone factory function.

Writing stone paint logic...

Still building terrain and wall logic...

Still writing helper functions...

I should guard against mutating shared geometry by generating fresh instances per part, then move on to finalizing the code while watching for unused-variable lint errors. I'm also sketching out placement for tiny glowing sparkle accents and underside crystal positions using angle and height arrays with polar coordinate helpers.

Still writing procedural rock generation...

Tree counts look fine, and I'll add a water pond with lilies. For the lantern, I'm designing a lathe-based stone body with a small glowing orange box light, a rotated cylinder roof, a gold finial, and a connecting plate, all positioned relative to the base height.

Typing outline arrays...

Defining pond ripple rings and gradient coloring, then placing rim stones around the pond radius while skipping the section near the river's azimuth direction.

I'm double-checking the API signatures for cel, card color options, and frame arrays to confirm types are compatible before writing the file.
